dossier.summary: Devin is represented as a Cognition-managed rolling hosted coding-agent service with dated Devin 2.2 and API v3 milestones, two documented enterprise deployment models, unresolved service and runtime revisions, and separately scoped plan, action, child-session and desktop-QA approval boundaries.

releaseContext.statement: Cognition's release notes pin Devin 2.2 on 2026-02-24 and the v3 API primary release on 2026-02-20. Subsequent dated updates demonstrate a rolling service, so neither milestone identifies the current Brain, Devbox, model or deployment revision.

limitations: All product claims are attributed to Cognition public sources; no behavior was observed.
No Devin account, service, API, session, model, Devbox, integration, tenant or outpost was installed, invoked or inspected.
Devin 2.2 and API v3 are dated service and API milestones, not immutable current service builds.
Enterprise Cloud and Customer Dedicated share a Cognition Cloud Brain but have different Devbox, tenant and network boundaries.
The API schema establishes selectable fields and status meanings, not their effective value in any session.
A service-user permission does not establish a particular session's target user, repository authority or audit attribution.
Plan approval, safe-mode action approval, approval bypass and desktop-QA approval are different gates and are not collapsed.
The desktop-QA approval claim is scoped to the Devin 2.2 release note and is not silently rolled forward.
GitHub App permissions are publisher-declared authorization requirements, not proof that any repository action occurred.
Secure Mode's stated effect does not identify a complete egress policy or prove enforcement.
The compound-system description does not identify an exact model or model-serving revision.
No independent evaluation passed independence, exact applicability, disclosure and public-artifact gates.
No performance, correctness, quality, safety, privacy, containment or approval-enforcement conclusion is supported.

propositions.question: Which Devin service or release identity does this record establish?
propositions.status: Rolling service; two dated milestones; current revision unresolved
propositions.answer: The record identifies the Devin hosted surface, the dated Devin 2.2 and API v3 milestones, and an unresolved current service revision.
propositions.whyItMatters: A named service milestone must not be substituted for the backend serving a later session.

propositions.question: Where do the Brain and Devbox run?
propositions.status: Two offering alternatives; exact revisions unresolved
propositions.answer: Cognition documents Enterprise Cloud and Customer Dedicated Devbox placements while saying the Brain remains in Cognition Cloud.
propositions.whyItMatters: Tenant, network and execution boundaries differ even when the product name is the same.

propositions.question: Which mode, platform and parent-child placement applied?
propositions.status: Selectable and inheritable; effective values unknown
propositions.answer: The v3 API exposes modes, explicit platforms or outpost pools, and parent placement inheritance, but this dossier has no session receipt.
propositions.whyItMatters: Mode and placement are runtime applicability boundaries independent of the service label.

propositions.question: Whose identity creates and owns a session?
propositions.status: Service-user, impersonated-user and beta PAT paths separated
propositions.answer: Cognition distinguishes service-user and human credentials and requires separate permissions when a service user creates a session on behalf of a human.
propositions.whyItMatters: Caller authority and session attribution are not the same identity boundary.

propositions.question: Which human approvals can occur before planning, actions and desktop QA?
propositions.status: Three distinct gates plus an explicit bypass configuration
propositions.answer: Current planning can auto-proceed after a feedback window or wait for explicit approval; safe mode can await action approval; publisher configuration guidance says bypass approval removes manual approval for named scheduled actions; Devin 2.2 separately requested approval before desktop QA.
propositions.whyItMatters: Approval authority is stage-specific and can change through configuration rather than forming one global yes-or-no control.

propositions.question: What GitHub access does Cognition say the integration requests?
propositions.status: Repository scope selectable; read/write permissions publisher-declared
propositions.answer: The GitHub App can be limited to selected repositories or granted all organization repositories and requests multiple read and read/write permissions, including contents, issues, pull requests and workflows.
propositions.whyItMatters: Integration installation scope and repository controls bound what a session can change.

propositions.question: Which network mode and model backend applied?
propositions.status: Secure Mode and compound-system claims; exact values unresolved
propositions.answer: A dated release note says Secure Mode removes native internet deployment capabilities, while current deployment docs describe Devin as a Cognition-managed compound system without third-party LLM keys.
propositions.whyItMatters: Neither statement identifies an effective egress policy or exact model for a session.

propositions.question: Was this exact hosted record independently evaluated?
propositions.answer: The audited Terminal-Bench references do not establish an exact Devin service revision, deployment, model, configuration, independent evaluator role and public run artifact for this record.
propositions.whyItMatters: Publisher claims and incompletely applicable benchmark references cannot be presented as observed behavior.
